Finding: Starting skills and finish-level competencies are not measurable.
Learner impact: Completing scripts can be confused with understanding ML or professional readiness.
Improvement: Define three outcomes: explain ML, complete a guided project, and complete an independent project. Assess each separately.
Completion check: A learner can name the evidence needed to finish each level.

Finding: Python setup precedes a basic computer-skills readiness unit.
Learner impact: Non-technical learners may stop before meeting an ML concept.
Improvement: Add folders, extensions, ZIP extraction, terminal prompts, saving text, CSV rows and running a command, with pictures and a checklist.
Completion check: A novice extracts, edits, saves and runs a lesson without help.

Finding: One Python-heavy route serves both technical builders and non-technical professionals.
Learner impact: People who need to evaluate an ML proposal must first become Python operators.
Improvement: Offer an explanation-and-spreadsheet route and a Python builder route, sharing concepts with different implementation depth.
Completion check: A professional can finish the literacy route without Python.

Finding: Core skips prerequisites later used in its capstone.
Learner impact: Imputation, encoding, problem definition and model selection can become unexplained machinery.
Improvement: Add a dependency map and promote selected preparation, encoding, baseline and model-choice lessons into Core.
Completion check: Every required skill is taught before it is used.

Location: Core table lesson 444; workbook lines 4017 and 8282
Finding: Core lesson 444 explicitly requires lesson 205, which is outside Core.
Learner impact: The advertised nine-lesson route is not self-contained.
Improvement: Include confusion-matrix reading before thresholds and probabilities.
Completion check: The learner counts false alarms and missed urgent orders before lesson 444.

Finding: Overfitting is optional before selecting and deploying a model.
Learner impact: A learner can reach deployment without understanding why low training error can mislead.
Improvement: Make the validation-curve lesson mandatory before model comparison.
Completion check: The learner rejects a memorizing model using validation evidence.

Location: Beginner path; Core course; Start here
Finding: Several competing starting sequences appear.
Learner impact: Beginner jumps 002 to 069 to 071; Core starts 002 to 032 to 055; 001 is also Start here.
Improvement: Label one primary route, a short demonstration and a reference library. Show the next step consistently.
Completion check: The homepage has one unambiguous full-course start.

Finding: Consistent workload, duration and stopping-point guidance is missing.
Learner impact: Students and busy professionals cannot plan study realistically.
Improvement: Pilot modules and publish reading and practice estimates separately; include suggested stopping points.
Completion check: Each required module states expected effort and a finish condition.

Finding: 447 numbered entries include headings and reused exercises; 311 entries have shared-exercise metadata.
Learner impact: The volume can overwhelm learners and obscure distinct practice.
Improvement: Present modules and distinct labs first. Distinguish a lab, a variation, a heading and a reference.
Completion check: The learner sees the actual number of required learning activities.

Location: PDF page map and PDF-derived headings
Finding: An unavailable PDF determines some naming and ordering.
Learner impact: References to the PDF interrupt standalone learning and preserve confusing classifications.
Improvement: Organize teaching by dependencies; keep historical heading/page mappings in an appendix with provenance.
Completion check: No required instruction depends on an absent PDF.

Finding: A glossary replaces a gradual Python introduction.
Learner impact: Assignment, lists, strings, methods, indexing and nested brackets arrive together.
Improvement: Add tiny runnable primers using delivery data for variables, lists, tables, row/column selection and functions.
Completion check: The learner explains the difference between a one-column table and a target series.

Finding: Setup uses a virtual-environment executable; workbook and ZIP commands revert to bare python.
Learner impact: A beginner can install and run in different interpreters.
Improvement: Use one consistent command convention and add an executable/version check.
Completion check: Installation and execution use the same environment.

Finding: Obtaining the complete folder is assumed.
Learner impact: A non-developer may download only HTML or one archive and miss adjacent assets.
Improvement: Provide a complete downloadable bundle, extraction walkthrough and expected folder tree without requiring Git.
Completion check: A new learner obtains a complete offline copy.

Location: SETUP.md CSV edits; all practice CSVs
Finding: Safe CSV editing is not taught.
Learner impact: Delimiters, quoting, headers, extensions and unsaved edits can break tasks.
Improvement: Show an edit in a text editor and spreadsheet, including blank cells and saving as CSV. Provide before/after examples.
Completion check: A learner edits a cell while preserving file format and headers.

Location: Mean, median, mode, IQR and z-score sections
Finding: Arithmetic prerequisites are not a structured just-in-time sequence.
Learner impact: Fractions, percentages, quartiles, averages and spread can obstruct the ML idea.
Improvement: Teach sorting, middle value, average, percentages and spread with five values before introducing the library methods.
Completion check: The learner manually calculates a median and percentage first.

Finding: Graph-reading skills are assumed.
Learner impact: Axes, units, one-dot-per-record and bins may be unfamiliar.
Improvement: Add one annotated scatterplot and histogram before technical figures, with questions read directly from the charts.
Completion check: The learner identifies a record, coordinates and units.

Finding: How fitting chooses a model remains hidden behind the first exact pattern.
Learner impact: The learner can call predict without understanding what was learned.
Improvement: Show minutes = 10 + 2 x distance, two wrong lines, the learned line and then a noisy record. Explain slope, intercept and error with numbers.
Completion check: The learner predicts 4 km by hand and explains why noisy data changes the fit.

Location: ML task categories and problem definition
Finding: There is no early mixed exercise choosing a task from a new question.
Learner impact: Number prediction, known categories and discovered groups can be confused.
Improvement: Sort ten everyday questions by output type and available feedback; provide reasons for the answers.
Completion check: The learner selects and justifies a task type for a new case.

Finding: Many advanced terms used in lessons lack glossary entries.
Learner impact: Regularization, hyperparameter, tensor, loss, optimizer, gradient, epoch and silhouette interrupt reading.
Improvement: Expand first-use definitions and link each to a small example. Mark advanced vocabulary as optional.
Completion check: Every required unfamiliar term is explained before use or directly linked.

Finding: Troubleshooting focuses on missing files and modules.
Learner impact: Invalid CSVs, ValueError, port conflicts and other common failures have no recovery path.
Improvement: Add an error-to-action decision tree with reversible fixes and restoring original files.
Completion check: A learner fixes an intentionally missing-column error without reinstalling Python.

Finding: The diagram supports 1 and false, but the mapping omits those strings.
Learner impact: Reproduced: both become NaN rather than known Boolean values.
Improvement: Use one complete normalized mapping for yes/true/1 and no/false/0; test unknown separately.
Completion check: All six known spellings convert correctly in both lessons.

Finding: The suggested edit changes February 1 to February 4, a date already present.
Learner impact: The script fails with cannot reindex on an axis with duplicate labels.
Improvement: Change a measurement instead, such as February 3 orders from 16 to 18. Teach duplicate timestamps separately.
Completion check: The documented experiment runs and changes the interpolated February 2 reading.

Finding: The CNN lesson promises a convolution; its script uses grayscale pixels and KNeighborsClassifier, with no convolution.
Learner impact: A learner can complete the CNN lesson without meeting a CNN.
Improvement: Rename it to image preprocessing for KNN, or supply an actual annotated convolution example and optional neural-network lab.
Completion check: Title, objective, code and output teach the same operation.

Finding: The Streamlit copy instruction leaves __TRAINING_CSV__ in the app string.
Learner impact: AppTest replaces the placeholder automatically, but copying the string literally does not.
Improvement: Ship a runnable delivery_app.py resolving its CSV relative to the file and give its exact launch command.
Completion check: The interactive app runs without manual code surgery.

Finding: The browser walkthrough says to paste two blocks, but the section contains no pair of app-code blocks.
Learner impact: The learner cannot follow the instruction as written.
Improvement: Refer to the supplied lesson.py app with the exact Uvicorn command, or ship a named web_delivery.py.
Completion check: The documented files and command open the described browser page.

Finding: Cloud storage and geocoding link to generic Flask-hosting, BI and web/mobile notes.
Learner impact: The promised manual walkthrough does not explain the named task.
Improvement: Supply topic-specific storage/geocoding instructions or describe these lessons as local-only illustrations.
Completion check: Every promised walkthrough actually covers its topic.

Finding: Equal feature values are treated as records that must not cross splits, without establishing common observation identity.
Learner impact: Independent deliveries can have the same rounded distance and weight; blanket removal teaches the wrong general leakage rule.
Improvement: Distinguish copied observations from independent records with equal inputs. Define grouping from identity, provenance or genuine dependencies, or explicitly teach a pair-held-out task.
Completion check: Independent equal-measurement shipments are accepted while duplicate shipment identity is blocked.

Location: Ordered label heading line 1879; LDA heading line 7333
Finding: Titles preserve misleading categories despite corrective prose: ordinal inputs are called label encoding, and supervised LDA sits under unsupervised learning.
Learner impact: Scanning learners can retain the wrong classification.
Improvement: Rename to ordinal feature encoding, separate target encoding of labels, and move LDA to supervised transformations.
Completion check: The table of contents is accurate without a later correction.

Finding: Some scripts reserve checking rows without evaluating them.
Learner impact: A partition in code can be mistaken for a completed model check.
Improvement: Use the reserved rows and print actual versus predicted outcomes, or explicitly label a transformation-only demonstration and remove unused partitions.
Completion check: Every reserved check set has a stated and executed check.

Finding: Some edits change features while retaining the old actual_minutes.
Learner impact: Changing a known 10 km delivery to 14 km leaves its previous observed outcome beside a hypothetical request.
Improvement: Clear actual outcomes for invented requests or state a deliberate synthetic assumption. Follow the clearer instruction already used in train-and-test.
Completion check: A hypothetical input is never silently scored against the old observation.

Finding: The ZIP changes button names; the workbook changes reward chances. The code learns from reward-chance row order rather than button names.
Learner impact: The archive experiment can leave the learned action unchanged for the wrong reason.
Improvement: Use the same probability-edit experiment and print action names with indices.
Completion check: Workbook and ZIP describe the same meaningful experiment.

Finding: The chi-square example uses elapsed minutes directly and mainly emphasizes nonnegativity.
Learner impact: Learners may infer that any nonnegative measurement is an appropriate count/frequency feature.
Improvement: Use count or indicator features for chi-square and a separately explained continuous-feature example for ANOVA; explain assumptions and units.
Completion check: The learner distinguishes count data from an arbitrary continuous measurement.

Finding: Training Boolean strings are lowercased without stripping spaces, while new-input strings are stripped first.
Learner impact: The same spelling with surrounding spaces can be treated differently in training and prediction.
Improvement: Use one shared normalization function for both paths; teach fixed transformations versus learned imputation.
Completion check: A whitespace-padded value has the same representation in training and inference.

Finding: Core teaches finding missing cells without requiring a basic complete imputation workflow.
Learner impact: The capstone then uses median imputation before the learner has demonstrated it.
Improvement: Add a required find-decide-fill-apply lab, including when not to fill and when to preserve a missingness flag.
Completion check: A fresh blank uses the training median without refitting on the request.

Location: Core route; one-hot lesson 075 outside Core
Finding: Core does not explicitly teach the categorical representation its capstone uses.
Learner impact: Zone indicators become unexplained machinery.
Improvement: Add a required paper-and-code one-hot lesson, including blank versus unseen categories.
Completion check: The learner constructs an encoded North row and explains an unseen-zone policy.

Finding: Scaling examples use unregularized linear regression, which can retain the same predictions under invertible rescaling.
Learner impact: Values change, but the learner may not see why scaling matters.
Improvement: Explain the unchanged prediction explicitly, then compare a distance-based or regularized model before and after scaling on common validation rows.
Completion check: The learner explains both an unchanged linear prediction and a changed distance-based prediction.

Finding: The transformation catalog is much larger than the decision guidance.
Learner impact: It can look like a cleaning checklist in which every method should be used.
Improvement: Add a table of issue, candidate, conditions, information changed and validation method. Include doing nothing.
Completion check: The learner chooses one candidate and explains why the others are unnecessary.

Finding: Splitting is taught after cleaning and feature selection, although many scripts correctly split first.
Learner impact: A learner following the chapter order can learn preprocessing statistics before reserving test rows.
Improvement: Teach prediction-time availability and split design early; separate fixed format conversions from learned preparation.
Completion check: The learner identifies which preparation operations learn from data and where each must be fitted.

Finding: Regularization lacks a worked account of penalties and scale.
Learner impact: Alpha can appear to be an arbitrary magic number.
Improvement: Compare coefficients and errors for ordinary, weakly penalized and strongly penalized fits. Explain unit-dependent penalties and scaling choices.
Completion check: The learner explains what increasing alpha changes.

Finding: Scores, ranking, calibration and yes/no decisions need a more gradual bridge.
Learner impact: A score such as 0.7 can be mistaken for certainty or a compulsory alert.
Improvement: Use ten scored examples to distinguish probability estimates, observed frequencies and decision cutoffs; teach calibration afterward.
Completion check: The learner changes a cutoff without claiming to have changed the model's estimated probabilities.

Location: First prediction and small synthetic examples
Finding: Noise and irreducible uncertainty are not a required learning progression.
Learner impact: Perfect patterns can make real-world errors look like programming mistakes.
Improvement: Add noise to the same relation, omit an influential feature and compare several possible outcomes for one input.
Completion check: The learner explains why identical inputs can have different actual delivery times.

Finding: Parsing is covered, but timezone, cyclic values and prediction timing are not joined into a usable workflow.
Learner impact: Learners may mix local/UTC time or treat midnight as far from 23:00.
Improvement: Add optional timezone and cyclic-hour examples and state timestamp meaning and prediction horizon.
Completion check: The learner identifies when a field becomes available and how midnight should be represented.

Finding: Cleanup is demonstrated more than its failure cases.
Learner impact: Lowercasing and punctuation removal can be applied as universal rules.
Improvement: Compare negation, punctuation, IDs and case-sensitive content. Explain task- and language-dependent choices.
Completion check: The learner gives an example where removing a symbol or token damages meaning.

Finding: Cluster counts and density settings are largely chosen for neat supplied groups.
Learner impact: Assigning a cluster is easier than judging whether useful groups exist.
Improvement: Add overlapping and no-cluster cases; compare K, DBSCAN settings, profiles and stability. Explain that silhouette is a clue rather than business validation.
Completion check: The learner can conclude that segmentation is not useful.

Location: Media, BERT, semi-supervised and RL sections
Finding: Advanced mechanisms lack a separate prerequisite curriculum.
Learner impact: Tensors, optimizers, loss, replay, pseudo-label objectives and search arrive far beyond the beginner preparation.
Improvement: Move them to electives with readiness checks. Add neural-network foundations before CNN/LSTM/DQN and distinguish mechanics from useful learned representations.
Completion check: Learners can skip electives without losing a Core outcome.

Finding: Most tasks ask learners to run and compare rather than predict and explain first.
Learner impact: Recognizing a supplied output can be mistaken for understanding.
Improvement: Use predict-run-explain-check in every required lab; reveal the answer after the prediction.
Completion check: The learner records and explains an expectation before execution.

Finding: Concept checkpoints with explained answers are not consistent.
Learner impact: Learners can advance with unresolved misconceptions.
Improvement: Add three to five short questions per module, explain plausible wrong answers and link to a specific relearning activity.
Completion check: Confusing train and test leads to a targeted exercise before advancing.

Finding: Support does not progressively fade toward construction.
Learner impact: Learners may finish many runs without building a workflow.
Improvement: Progress from worked example to fill-in task to starter script to an unseen case.
Completion check: The final project begins with a brief and dictionary rather than a complete solution.

Finding: The useful capstone rubric mostly checks a supplied implementation.
Learner impact: Reporting the printed winner and error does not demonstrate independent choices.
Improvement: Retain the current guided capstone; add a second unseen case requiring a split, baseline, evaluation and decision memo.
Completion check: An independent project justifies every major decision.

Finding: There is no structured retrieval or mixed-practice cycle.
Learner impact: Knowledge can remain tied to a filename or example.
Improvement: Add cumulative quizzes and later mixed tasks that revisit missingness, leakage and metrics in another domain.
Completion check: The learner solves a mixed task later without rereading the solution.

Location: Generic edits in lessons 027, 059, 104, 171 and related entries
Finding: Some experiments change IDs instead of the concept being taught.
Learner impact: An output can change cosmetically while the model stays the same.
Improvement: Use concept-specific edits and state both expected changes and expected invariants.
Completion check: Every task has a reasoned learning observation, including deliberately unchanged results.

Finding: All exercises use invented data; most early practice is tiny.
Learner impact: No required bridge develops competence with unfamiliar messy and representative data.
Improvement: Keep synthetic examples; add a documented real-data project or unseen realistic benchmark with appropriate size and limitations.
Completion check: The learner audits and models data not tailored to reveal the intended answer.

Location: One/two-row checks and many near-perfect classification examples
Finding: Cautions about tiny examples exist, but performance uncertainty is not demonstrated as a required task.
Learner impact: Small numerical differences may still be treated as dependable winners.
Improvement: Use repeated sampling or resampling to illustrate score variation, reporting counts alongside scores. Explain methodological limits.
Completion check: The learner refuses to declare a reliable winner from two cases or a negligible difference.

Finding: Separate algorithm test results can invite selecting by repeatedly inspecting test scores.
Learner impact: That weakens the final-test discipline taught elsewhere.
Improvement: Provide one common validation comparison and one untouched final evaluation; label catalog scores as demonstrations rather than a leaderboard.
Completion check: The learner selects the method before looking at its final test result.

Finding: Average errors receive more development than rare large mistakes.
Learner impact: Low MAE can conceal unacceptable individual errors.
Improvement: Add an error percentile, worst-case inspection and a practical tolerance such as within five minutes; keep interval estimation optional.
Completion check: The learner reports sample count, average error and one measure of large misses.

Finding: Core does not require deciding whether ML is needed.
Learner impact: A model may replace a simpler sufficient rule or process improvement.
Improvement: Require a brief covering decision, users, information available, existing process, simple alternative, success threshold and owner.
Completion check: The learner can justify a non-ML solution.

Finding: Metrics need a stronger connection to costs and team workload.
Learner impact: A high-recall cutoff can create more alerts than the team can handle.
Improvement: Add validation-based choices using miss cost, false-alarm cost and review capacity.
Completion check: The learner justifies a cutoff using both model results and operational limits.

Finding: The runnable privacy exercise mainly removes a contact column, and fairness is not developed into a task.
Learner impact: Professionals need permitted-use, harm and ownership decisions as well as preprocessing.
Improvement: Add a proportionate project worksheet on permissions, minimization, retention, access, subgroup harms and human review. Verify jurisdiction-specific references if included.
Completion check: The brief names a data owner, intended use, retention decision and harm review.

Finding: Sampling coverage and label quality are not a complete audit workflow.
Learner impact: A clean file can be unrepresentative or have inconsistent outcomes.
Improvement: Define population, inclusion rules, label meaning/timing, disagreement and coverage.
Completion check: The learner identifies an underrepresented case and a questionable label before training.

Finding: The correct warning that importance is not causal lacks a transfer exercise.
Learner impact: Predictive dependence can still become an unsupported intervention claim.
Improvement: Compare correlation, model reliance and experimental evidence; ask learners to state what cannot be concluded.
Completion check: The learner rejects an intervention claim supported only by prediction.

Finding: Professional handoff information is partial and scattered.
Learner impact: Another person needs purpose, limitations, evaluation, ownership and recovery instructions.
Improvement: Extend the existing metadata with a readable model card, data summary, decision log and service handoff.
Completion check: Another learner reproduces the project and explains when predictions should be declined.

Finding: Investigation is taught well, but no complete incident-response exercise follows an alert.
Learner impact: The learner may not know what to do next or how to accept a replacement.
Improvement: Add source investigation, temporary fallback, new labels, later-data candidate comparison and a recorded promotion/rejection decision.
Completion check: The learner provides an incident response with an owner and fallback.

Finding: This is primarily classical ML rather than a complete modern AI-literacy curriculum.
Learner impact: Marketing it as all of AI would leave gaps around generative AI, pretrained models and retrieval.
Improvement: Keep the ML scope explicit. If broader AI literacy is intended, add a separate orientation without bloating beginner Core.
Completion check: Published outcomes state exactly which kinds of AI are covered.

Location: Dataset headings Titanic, Iris, MNIST, Fashion MNIST, Boston Housing
Finding: Prominent famous-dataset names label different invented data, schemas and sometimes tasks.
Learner impact: Scanning readers can misunderstand provenance despite the explicit synthetic-data note.
Improvement: Name lessons after the actual invented ferry, flower, digit or neighborhood exercise; retain historical mappings as metadata.
Completion check: The title communicates the actual data source and task.

Location: Offline HTML setup and glossary links
Finding: Offline companion links open raw Markdown files.
Learner impact: A browser may show or download plain text rather than formatted guidance.
Improvement: Bundle readable setup/glossary HTML and point local links to those pages.
Completion check: Offline use needs no Markdown viewer.

Location: HTML single-page workbook and Core links
Finding: Scroll progress is provided, but not lesson-completion or competency progress.
Learner impact: Learners cannot reliably resume the next unfinished activity.
Improvement: Add a printable checklist or optional local tracker keyed to checkpoints and exercises.
Completion check: The learner resumes the next unfinished learning step after closing the page.

Finding: Much explanatory text lives inside raster figures, although alt text and adjacent explanations are already present.
Learner impact: Selection, translation, small-screen enlargement and some accessibility workflows are harder.
Improvement: Keep essential text selectable, add plot data tables, and test keyboard/screen-reader use. Preserve existing good alt text and responsive behavior.
Completion check: Essential teaching conclusions remain understandable without the image.

Finding: Windows/macOS clean installs are explicitly unverified.
Learner impact: Non-technical learners need a dependable route on their own OS.
Improvement: Test Core from clean supported environments on each advertised OS and record commands, versions and recovery guidance.
Completion check: A fresh-machine run passes the required route on every supported platform.

Location: Core pins versus broad ZIP requirement ranges
Finding: Fresh per-lesson installs can differ from the recorded environment.
Learner impact: Reproduction can depend on newer dependency combinations rather than the teaching recipe.
Improvement: Provide one constrained beginner environment and separate optional groups with an update policy.
Completion check: A learner can recreate the supported environment and identify optional dependencies before installation.

Location: Archive-only distribution in this folder; README validation limits
Finding: No included release harness verifies all documented experiments.
Learner impact: Default snapshots do not catch a failing suggested edit such as lesson 101.
Improvement: Maintain editable source and a repeatable build checking ZIP contents, links, syntax, default runs and documented mutations.
Completion check: The Boolean and duplicate-date regressions fail release checks.

Location: No learner study or instructor guide supplied in this folder
Finding: Beginner independence has not been demonstrated by evidence included with the course.
Learner impact: Expert review identifies likely obstacles but cannot measure real novice success.
Improvement: Pilot with several never-coded learners, observe their explanations and blockers, measure tasks and provide instructor hints and answer explanations.
Completion check: Observed beginners complete the required route and an independent transfer task; unresolved barriers are recorded.
